results.fact: Where the Honeymoon gully leaves the main slope
results.correct_value: The Honeymoon gully branches left off the main snow slope before (short of) the Deception-Martin low point; parties should not climb to the ridge crest first.
results.evidence: A 2007 Honeymoon-route trip report says not to bother climbing to the ridgeline, but to go straight at the prominent snow gully (its party did reach the ridge and had to drop back down to the gully, costing time). The SummitPost description of the variation says it climbs nearly to the low point and then takes a left-branching snow gully. Both agree with approach and baseFinding; pitch_detail[1] alone had the party dropping off the low point.

patches.find: Drop off the low point of the Deception-Martin ridge into a steep, left-branching snow gully
patches.replace: Climb nearly to the low point of the Deception-Martin ridge, then branch left into the steep side gully
patches.fact: Where the Honeymoon gully leaves the main slope

results.correct_value: Trailhead parking pass for day trips; an overnight wilderness permit costs a $6 reservation fee plus $8 per person (16+) per night.
results.evidence: The park's wilderness reservations page states a $6 non-refundable reservation fee per overnight permit plus $8 per person per night for ages 16 and older. Washington's National Park Fund's permit guide gives the same $6 and $8 figures. The fees line claiming nothing is due beyond parking is wrong for overnight trips.

patches.find: None beyond the trailhead parking pass this route already lists.
patches.replace: The trailhead parking pass for a day climb; an overnight adds the wilderness permit — a $6 reservation fee plus $8 per person (16 and older) per night.

results.fact: Distance and gain to Upper Royal Basin
results.correct_value: Royal Lake is 7.2 mi and ~2,500 ft from the trailhead; Upper Royal Basin is about 8 mi one-way (16 mi RT), ~500 ft above the lake.
results.evidence: WTA gives Royal Lake at 7.2 mi and the upper basin three-quarters of a mile beyond, 16.0 mi round trip. A second hiking guide gives 7.2 mi and 2,500 ft to Royal Lake and 8 mi to Upper Royal Basin, another mile and 500 ft past the lake; the park's Royal Basin page gives 7.2 mi to the lake. Partner requirements' 7 mi / 14 mi RT to the upper basin is the lake figure.

results.correct_value: Late June to early July, while snow still covers the loose upper rock; July 1 is the usual cut-off before the rock becomes very loose.
results.evidence: The Mazamas route page says early-season climbing before July 1 is strongly preferred to avoid very loose rock. The SummitPost page puts the best time in early July, while snow still covers most of the route and the camps have melted out. Both tie the window to snow cover at the turn of June/July; best_season's 'early-to-mid July' contradicted its own next sentence and the itinerary/approach 'before July' advice.

patches.find: Early-to-mid July is generally the prime window
patches.replace: Late June to early July is generally the prime window

results.evidence: Climber Kyle and the standard description call the route class 2 (class 2 slopes to the summit after the Gilhooley traverse), while other climbers argue the scree slope to the ridge needs hands and is class 3 minimum; the Mazamas rate it by their own letter scale. No two sources agree on a single 'Class 2-3' rating for the whole route. A current guidebook rating for the standard route would settle it.

results.correct_value: Two or three days is typical (2 days for strong parties, 3 common).
results.evidence: The Mazamas run it car to car in two or more days and suggest a 3-day weekend when paired with Mystery; a Climber Kyle trip was a 3-day backpack.
